title: Polymers and Biomolecules: The Chemistry of Giants

questions.question: In the term 'polymer', the repeating small units are called:
questions.rationale: Polymers are built from monomers linked end to end, the way ethylene units chain into polyethylene.

questions.question: Nylon is formed by joining adipic acid and hexamethylenediamine with the loss of water. This is an example of:
questions.rationale: In condensation polymerisation, monomers with complementary functional groups join, releasing a small molecule — usually water — per bond formed.

questions.question: Which type of plastic softens on heating and can be remoulded repeatedly?
questions.rationale: Thermoplastics (PE, PP, PVC, PET) have linear or branched chains that slide apart on heating; thermosets are permanently cross-linked and only char.

questions.question: Vulcanisation of natural rubber involves heating it with:
questions.rationale: Goodyear's vulcanisation forms sulphur cross-links between rubber chains; the degree of cross-linking spans elastic bands to tyre rubber to hard ebonite.

questions.question: The first fully synthetic plastic, made from phenol and formaldehyde in 1907, was:
questions.rationale: Bakelite, a thermosetting phenol-formaldehyde resin created by Leo Baekeland, was the first completely synthetic plastic.

questions.question: Humans cannot digest cellulose because we lack the enzyme to break its β-glucose linkages. Which polysaccharide CAN we digest?
questions.rationale: Starch uses α-glucose bonds, which amylase can cleave; cellulose's β linkages pass through us as dietary fibre.

questions.question: Amino acids in a protein are joined by:
questions.rationale: Peptide bonds (a condensation link between the amino group of one amino acid and the acid group of the next) form the protein's primary chain.

questions.question: Why does frying an egg turn the transparent white opaque and solid?
options: Heat denatures the proteins, destroying their folded shape
questions.rationale: Denaturation unravels and tangles the folded proteins into a solid network — the shape (and so the function) is lost permanently.

questions.question: In DNA, adenine pairs across the helix with:
questions.rationale: A–T and G–C pairing via hydrogen bonds; uracil replaces thymine only in RNA.

questions.question: Which fibre, used in bulletproof vests, is about five times stronger than steel by weight?
questions.rationale: Kevlar, an aramid polymer, owes its strength to rigid, highly ordered chains packed with hydrogen bonds between them.
